newsitem.title: UK: Safeway, BP in shopping joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Safeway, BP in shopping joint venture.

text.p: British supermarket retailer Safeway Plc and oil company British Petroleum (BP) said they were setting up a 50:50 joint venture to spend 100 million stg on developing food and fuel sites in the UK.
The companies said around 100 sites were envisaged.
The petrol retailing and forecourt business will be BP-branded and the shopping stores will carry Safeway's logo, the companies said.
Profits from the joint venture will be shared between the two partners.
A pilot site with a Safeway store of 2,000 square feet will be opened next month in Basildon, Essex, with further sites planned for early 1997.
Subject to their success, the companies said, a full scale countrywide construction programme would be started.
Sites will be selected from the network of over 2,000 service stations created by the recent merger of BP and Mobil's European retail business.
"We believe there is a rapidly growing demand for this style of combined retail outlet," said Rolf Stomberg, chief executive of BP Oil.
